title: Pandya Empire
capsule: The 'Pandya Empire' phase (1216-1326) covers the dynasty's second and greatest rise to imperial power under Maravarman Sundara Pandya I, who from 1216 defeated the Cholas and seized Uraiyur and Thanjavur, and above all under Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I (r. 1251-1268), whose armies campaigned into Sri Lanka, the Hoysala domains and the Kakatiya kingdom, making Madurai the paramount power of southern India. His successor Maravarman Kulasekara Pandya I (r. 1268-1308) held this ascendancy for four decades, but his death in 1308 touched off a fratricidal war between his sons Vira Pandya and Sundara Pandya that invited repeated Delhi Sultanate invasions, including Malik Kafur's sack of Madurai in 1311 and the 1323 conquest by Ulugh Khan, the future Muhammad bin Tughluq, which reduced the empire to a rump in its far-southern homeland around Tirunelveli and Tenkasi.

attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Pandya core territory around Madurai is well attested from inscriptions; the full extent of their dominion during the 13th-century expansion is less precisely mapped.
